Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp.'s Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; John Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; David Patel, VP of Exploration; Emily Vargas, VP of Marketing; Robert Kline, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Anna Novak, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Reynolds.

Mike Reynolds: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp. delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust production growth with better-than-expected well performance and accelerated new wells coming online. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on EBITDA expansion, fueled by higher volumes, stronger realizations, and sharp cost controls. We are focused on maintaining disciplined capital spending across drilling, completions, and facilities while coming in under budget. Further, we are working on advancing our refining operations with high throughput and superior margins. We continue to adjust to dynamic market conditions through effective hedging that protected our downside. We are advancing our exploration efforts and reserve bookings with strong replacement ratios. We are evaluating expansive future development opportunities across our tier-one acreage. Finally, we are taking steps to drive down lifting costs through innovative initiatives that are yielding tangible results.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Harlan to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Harlan: Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $2.5 billion, up 25% year-over-year. Operating income was $800 million, and net income was $550 million. We generated $950 million in free cash flow and returned $400 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $3.5 billion in debt and $1.2 billion in cash.

Let me expand on some key financial highlights. Starting with adjusted EBITDA, which came in at $1.65 billion for the quarter, representing a robust 38% year-over-year increase from $1.20 billion in Q3 2023. On a trailing twelve-month basis, this brings our adjusted EBITDA to a record $6.4 billion, up 45% YoY. This performance underscores our relentless focus on operational excellence, capital discipline, and capturing upside in a resilient hydrocarbon market.

Production volumes were the standout contributor, delivering over 60% of the YoY EBITDA lift. We averaged 285,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in Q3, a 22% increase from 234,000 boe/d last year. Oil volumes specifically grew 25% to 210,000 bbl/d, driven by our flagship Permian Basin assets, where we brought online 45 new horizontal wells across the Delaware and Midland sub-basins. These wells featured extended laterals averaging 12,500 feet—up from 10,000 feet in 2023—enabled by our proprietary multi-stage fracking designs and enhanced proppant loading, which boosted initial production rates by 18% per well to over 1,800 boe/d. In the Eagle Ford, our infill drilling program added another 15,000 boe/d, leveraging high-BTU associated gas to capitalize on soaring Henry Hub prices.

Offsetting some U.S. onshore strength, our Bakken position saw a modest 5% volume dip to 35,000 boe/d due to temporary curtailments from third-party midstream bottlenecks amid record regional flaring reductions. Internationally, Guyana offshore ramped ahead of schedule, contributing 12,000 boe/d from our 20% stake in Block X—mirroring ExxonMobil's Liza Phase 2 success—with first oil from our Yellowtail development now on track for Q4 2025.

Realized pricing added another 25% to the EBITDA bridge. Our realized oil price strengthened to $78.50 per barrel, up 17% YoY from $67.20, tracking the WTI benchmark's $76 average amid OPEC+ production cuts and geopolitical tightness in the Middle East. Natural gas realizations popped 35% to $3.85 per Mcf, fueled by U.S. LNG export demand outpacing domestic supply—think Cheniere's Corpus Christi Stage 3 hyper-chilling tech pulling in global cargoes. We realized a modest $1.20 per bbl hedge lift from our conservative 40% oil hedge book at a $70 floor, protecting downside while preserving upside exposure.

On the cost side, we shaved 15% off our cash operating costs, contributing the balance of the EBITDA growth. Lease operating expenses dropped to $7.80 per boe from $9.20, thanks to our fleet-wide adoption of digital oilfield initiatives, including AI-driven predictive maintenance on ESPs and rod-lift systems, which cut unplanned downtime by 28%. Lifting costs in the Permian specifically fell to $6.50/boe via centralized water management—recycling 75% of produced water onsite—and our shift to lower-emission electric frack fleets, aligning with ESG mandates from BlackRock and Vanguard clients. DD&A held steady at $14.50/boe, reflecting reserve additions from our 140 MMboe drilling inventory update.

Regionally, the Permian was the powerhouse at 65% of our EBITDA mix, generating $1.1 billion—up 55% YoY—on the back of D&C efficiency gains and peer-leading returns north of 60% IRR at current strips. Eagle Ford added $300 million, while international and Bakken rounded out the portfolio with diversified cash flow streams, mitigating WTI-Brent backwardation impacts.

Turning to our capital expenditures for the quarter, focusing on Drilling, Completion, and Facilities—our core D&C categories—comparing budget versus actual spend. For the full year 2024, we guided $2.4 billion in total capex, with roughly 45% allocated to Drilling, 35% to Completion, and 20% to Facilities and infrastructure. This reflects our disciplined approach: prioritizing longer laterals—now averaging 12,000 feet in the Delaware Basin—multi-well pads, and cube developments to optimize capital efficiency. Year-to-date through Q3, we've deployed $1.8 billion against a $1.9 billion budget, putting us under by about 5%, or $100 million. This variance is driven by operational efficiencies outweighing some inflationary pressures in services.

Starting with Drilling, which represents the largest slice at 45% of the program. Our Q3 budget was $280 million, reflecting 22 turn-in-line wells across five pads in the Waha and Midland sub-basins. Actual spend came in at $245 million—12% under budget, or $35 million saved. This outperformance stems from our adoption of rotary steerable systems combined with high-performance PDC bits from Schlumberger's NeoSteer platform, shaving average drilling days per 10,000-foot lateral from 18 days in 2023 to just 14 days—a 22% cycle time reduction. We're now routinely hitting ROP over 150 feet per hour in the Wolfcamp A and B benches. We've optimized our rig fleet with Patterson-UTI's PITech 1600 rigs, featuring automated catwalks and top drives that cut connection times by 30%. Drilling costs per lateral foot are down 15% YoY to $650.

Moving to Completion, our 35% bucket at $210 million budgeted for Q3, tied to fracking 25 wells with 60-stage designs. Actuals hit $225 million—7% over budget, or $15 million incremental—due to proppant and fluid inflation, with sand costs up 8% QoQ. Efficiencies elsewhere mitigated: our switch to Halliburton's SmartFleet electric fracs—now 80% of our program—reduced emissions by 50% and diesel burn by 40%. Completion costs per lateral foot rose only 3% YoY to $1,200.

Facilities at 20% of capex, budgeted at $120 million for Q3. Actual spend was $85 million—29% under, or $35 million deferred—reflecting strategic timing: we pushed out water management infrastructure in the Bakken due to third-party deals with Crestwood Equity Partners. Permian facilities focus on compression and gas processing upgrades.

Now, let's turn to our lifting costs per BOE, a core operational metric. In Q3, company-wide lifting costs—or LOE—came in at $7.85 per BOE, a 12% sequential improvement from $8.92 in Q2 and 28% year-over-year decline from $10.95 in Q3 2022. This marks the sixth consecutive quarter of double-digit reductions. Permian led at $7.15/BOE, Eagle Ford at $8.30/BOE, Bakken at $9.20/BOE, and GoM shelf at $11.00/BOE.

Powering these are our 'LiftLow 2025' initiatives targeting sub-$6.50/BOE by year-end. Digital twins via Halliburton’s DecisionSpace 360 cut unplanned downtime by 35%. Artificial lift optimization shifted 40% of Permian to gas-lift, dropping energy intensity by 22%. Water management recycling hit 65%. Supply chain contracts with SLB and Baker Hughes at 10% below peaks. Electrification pilots offset 30% diesel use. M&A synergies added scale.

On proved reserves additions, we added 285 million BOE to PDP and PDNP reserves, net of 192 MMboe production, for a total reserve replacement ratio of 148%. Organic RRR was 112%, ninth year above 100%. U.S. onshore contributed 210 MMboe, Permian 145 MMboe from 65 Wolfcamp/Bone Spring wells with P90 EURs over 1.2 MMboe. Bakken added 45 MMboe, international 55 MMboe including Thunder Horse South and Buzzard CO2-EOR.

Finally, our refining segment delivered robust performance. Average gross throughput was 2.42 million bpd, up 4% sequentially, at 93% utilization—highest in peers. Gulf Coast at 1.28 million bpd, Europe Rotterdam 420,000 bpd, Asia 720,000 bpd. Gross refining margin hit $18.20/bbl, up 12% QoQ, driven by 3:2:1 cracks at $22.50/bbl. Cash operating costs fell to $5.80/bbl, clean product yield 96.8%. Refining generated $1.8 billion EBITDA.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen for an operational update.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, John. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 285,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Permian Delaware Basin wells online, which are expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives, including those driving our lifting cost trends and operational efficiencies across regions.

Now I will turn it over to David Patel for an update on our exploration activities.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and are planning to drill multiple exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

As we look ahead, our future development plans are anchored in a disciplined, high-return portfolio. Independent reserves audit confirms year-end 2023 PDP reserves of 2.1 billion BOE, total 1P at 4.8 billion, 2P at 7.2 billion, 3P at 10.5 billion—a 12% 2P increase YoY. Net resource upside over 15 billion BOE unrisked, risked mean 4.2 billion. F&D at $8.50/BOE.

We're guiding 8-10% CAGR production growth to over 900,000 BOE/d by 2028, 2024 capex $4.2 billion. Permian 450,000 net acres, 25,000 locations, "Permian-X" program targeting 350,000 BOE/d by 2026. Offshore Guyana 30% WI, Karamat-1 discovery, 1.2 billion BOE contingent, Phase 2 FID. North Sea Judy/Joanne redevelopment, Mozambique LNG FID H2 2024.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Emily Vargas to discuss our marketing strategy.

Emily Vargas: Thank you, David. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for refined products in Gulf Coast and Asia markets, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of our high distillate yields and export arbitrage is significant, supporting premium realizations.

I will now turn it over to Robert Kline to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Emily. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. We have made significant progress on reducing our greenhouse gas emissions through electric fracs targeting 50% by year-end, slashing Scope 1 by 30%, water recycling at 75%, and CCS pilots with Occidental's STRATOS. We are also investing in renewable energy like solar microgrids, blue hydrogen, and renewable diesel at Sikka targeting 20,000 bpd by 2025. Improving water management and protecting biodiversity via electrification and low-carbon initiatives.

I will now turn the call over to Anna Novak to discuss our technology initiatives.

Anna Novak: Thank you, Robert. We are leveraging technology to improve our operational efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance safety. We are investing in automation, data analytics, and artificial intelligence—like AI reservoir simulation with Halliburton reducing uncertainty 25%, digital twins, Petrel models for 10-15% NDR uplift, AspenTech optimizers capturing $450 million YTD. We are also exploring carbon capture and storage, predictive maintenance cutting downtime 28-35%.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Ramirez with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on production guidance for next quarter and full year, including factors influencing projections?

John Harlan: Thanks, John. Happy to dive into our production guidance for Q4 2024 and the full year, along with key factors. We're guiding to remain disciplined amid volatility, balancing growth with efficiency.

For Q4, we're projecting 260,000 to 270,000 Mboe/d, a 4% sequential increase from Q3's 252 Mboe/d. Oil 185,000-195,000 bbl/d, NGLs 45,000-50,000 bbl/d, gas 180-210 MMcf/d. Full-year narrowing to 280,000-295,000 Mboe/d, up from prior 275,000-300,000, reflecting strong well performance and accelerated TILs offsetting weather deferrals.

Key drivers: D&C ramping with 12 operated rigs—eight Permian Delaware, three Eagle Ford, one Bakken. Q4 brings 45-50 DUCs online, 35 gross TILs in Permian, 12,000-ft laterals, super-lateral designs at 2,500 lbs/ft proppant, 30-day IPs 1,400 boe/d, EURs 1.4 MMboe/mile matching Pioneer/Occidental.

Permian 65% output, base declines 8-10% via refracs in Second White Specks. Eagle Ford oil cuts 65% with waterflood pilots expanding to 20 sections. Bakken 750 bbl/d IP30s hedged on Dakota Access.

Digital AI reservoir sim with Halliburton cuts uncertainty 25%, spacing to 450 ft for 1.5x inventory life.

Headwinds: declines 12-14%, Q3 South Texas weather deferred 5 Mboe/d to Q4, BLM methane rules/New Mexico setbacks mitigated by 50% electric fracs. Guyana Stabroek 15% stake deferred to 2027.

Supportive markets: WTI $80+, Brent $85, Henry Hub $2.75 underpin $45 Permian/$35 Eagle Ford breakevens. OPEC+ cuts, LNG ramps bolster 60% 2025 gas hedges at $3.00.

Prioritizing returns: 75% FCF to debt/dividends, DUCs to 250. ESG net-zero 2040 with STRATOS pilots.

Sets up $1.8 billion levered FCF, 20%+ ROIC.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Bennett with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Laura Bennett: Good morning. What are your expectations for realized prices going forward?

John Harlan: Good morning, Laura. Our hedging remains disciplined at 50-70% oil, 40-60% gas coverage 12-24 months. Q3 oil realized $76.45/bbl, gas $3.25/Mcf, with hedges adding $2.35/bbl oil, $0.45/Mcf gas. Hedge book: H2 2024 oil 62% at $71.80 swaps/$68-84 collars, 2025 45% $69.50/$65-82; gas similar. Added 200k bbls/month 2025 collars post-OPEC. Locks $85 million YTD gains, supports $45/BOE breakevens.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Ellis with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Ellis: Could you please provide more color on refining segment performance?

John Harlan: Absolutely, Tom. Refining throughput 2.42 million bpd at 93% utilization, GRM $18.20/bbl on $22.50 3:2:1 cracks. Processed sweet/heavy crudes, strong distillate yields 48%. Costs $5.80/bbl, yield 96.8%. Outperformed peers via trading, exports 450k bpd. Q4 moderate to 2.35-2.40 million bpd on turnarounds, hedging 60% at $20 floors. $1.8 billion EBITDA, 22% ROIC.

Operator: Our next question comes from Karen Soto with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Karen Soto: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

David Patel: Great question, Karen. Exploration successes bolster our 15 billion BOE upside, funding 8-10% growth to 900k BOE/d. Permian-X, Guyana Phase 2, North Sea redevelopment, Mozambique LNG integrate into strategy for 15-20% ROCE, 25% resource conversion.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel: What is the outlook for the new product in the coming years?

Emily Vargas: Mike, our refined products outlook is bright with diesel/jet demand, Asia premia, renewable diesel ramp to 20k bpd 2025. Export growth, ISCC certification for $2-4/bbl premia.

Operator: Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Rachel Kim: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Robert Kline: Yes, Rachel. Net-zero 2040 pathway: 25% Scope 1 cut by 2026, 50% electric fracs, 75% water recycle, CCS 2 Mtpa North Sea, solar offsets 30% diesel. OGCI aligned, low-CI exports.

Operator: Our next question comes from Derek Wong with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Derek Wong: What are the key technology initiatives you are focused on?

Anna Novak: Derek, key focuses: AI sims, digital twins cutting dry risk <5%, LP optimizers $450MM value, predictive maint 35% downtime cut, Delfi platform for infills.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Mike Reynolds for closing remarks.

Mike Reynolds: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
